Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.recorder

Class RecorderBackend

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.apps.recorder.RecorderBackend
public final class RecorderBackend extends Object
The AWT-free recording seam. Audio capture is genuinely native: the JDK's javax.sound.sampled opens the default capture line and writes PCM WAV on its own, so microphone recording needs no external tool. Screen (video) capture has no in-JDK encoder, so - exactly like the audio player's codec split and the Media Writer's dd/xorriso handoff - this backend builds the precise ffmpeg (or avconv) command line that grabs the X11 display, while the panel keeps the native javax.sound path for audio.

Every method here is pure and side-effect free - no process is started, no capture device is opened - so the whole command / format table is unit-testable headless. The thin process launch and TargetDataLine capture live in RecorderPanel, guarded like the desktop's other external-command paths.

    • wavFormat

      public static AudioFormat wavFormat(int sampleRate, int channels)
      The PCM signed 16-bit little-endian WAV format javax.sound.sampled writes natively. Building an AudioFormat touches no device, so this is safe to call headless.
      Parameters:
      sampleRate - the capture rate in Hz (clamped to 8000..192000)
      channels - 1 for mono, 2 for stereo (clamped to 1..2)
      Returns:
      the linear-PCM format

    • screenCommand

      public static List<String> screenCommand(String recorder, String output, String source, String resolution, int fps, boolean captureAudio)
      Builds the command line that records the X11 display with recorder. An optional microphone track is muxed in via PulseAudio when captureAudio is set.
      Parameters:
      recorder - the executable name (e.g. ffmpeg)
      output - the destination file path (typically .mp4)
      source - the X11 grab source (e.g. :0.0)
      resolution - a WIDTHxHEIGHT grab size, or null/blank for the whole screen
      fps - the frame rate (clamped to 1..120)
      captureAudio - true to also record the default microphone
      Returns:
      the argument list, never null; empty when a required input is blank
